claim: The tested SigLA snapshot decodes to 802 documents and 5,144 attestations.
limitations: Not epigraphic correctness.

claim: Two separately implemented executable decoding paths agreed on all 5,144 attestations across 46,296 compared fields on the same snapshot.
limitations: Not literal execution of both unmodified source trees; not GORILA agreement.

claim: The serialized SigLA document graph contains 1,401 Word objects, 1,283 nonempty and 118 empty.
limitations: Word is SigLA's source-defined unit; no linguistic semantics beyond source definition.

claim: Six checked current SigLA pages agree with decoded Word counts.
limitations: Six-page validation sample, not exhaustive manual review.

claim: Twenty-two source-word positional sign cases passed the 0.7 within-word permutation BH-FDR screen.
limitations: Model-dependent structural enrichment.

claim: Twelve of those 22 survived the 0.8 strict adversarial composite screen.
limitations: Composite screen chosen as robustness test; not probability of morphology.

claim: The displayed historical type-level table reports twelve frozen candidates; its Holm arithmetic was checked separately. The historical internal-position negative control is superseded.
limitations: The superseded negative control is not supporting evidence; selection on the same corpus precludes an independent confirmation claim.

claim: f3 has a stable evidence-tiered structural representation but unresolved global semantics.
limitations: Must not be used as universal word coordinates.

claim: The inherited 0.6 site_id was a document-label-prefix heuristic and is not canonical site metadata.
limitations: Canonical source-explicit site mapping remains future work.

claim: Independent identity-level replication of the twelve positional candidates has not yet been established.
limitations: Methodological comparators exist; exact independent replication not claimed.

claim: Known-answer Linear B calibration of this exact detector is not included in 1.0.
limitations: Requires a license-reviewed aligned Linear B word corpus.

claim: All twelve frozen positional candidates survived leave-one-canonical-site-out sensitivity in the 1.1 mapped source-word corpus.
limitations: Site mapping is reviewed identifier mapping; direct raw find-place per-record provenance remains an enhancement.

claim: All twelve frozen candidates reproduced their enriched boundary direction at type-level z > 1.96 in the pinned mwenge cross-representation corpus.
limitations: Not independent epigraphic replication; important shared GORILA/Douros ancestry.

claim: Eleven of twelve frozen candidates participate in at least two attested one-edge-removal type pairs.
limitations: Does not establish stems, affixes, paradigms or morphology.

claim: 6 of twelve frozen candidates retain a document-cluster-bootstrap 2.5th-percentile enrichment z > 1.96.
limitations: Corpus-composition sensitivity, not linguistic confidence interval.

claim: The source-word type graph contains 651 directed one-edge-removal relations versus a within-type-shuffle null mean of 587.2.
limitations: Order-sensitive form structure; not a test of morphological interpretation.

claim: Known-answer Linear B calibration remains unexecuted: exact source bytes are authenticated, but legitimate linguistic gold and the required graphical baseline remain missing.
evidence: Linear-B current-status and gold acquisition gate
limitations: Acquisition completion is not calibration performance; conventional transcription is not graphical sign identity.

claim: The historical 0.9 random-internal-position negative control is superseded because boundary and internal-position populations have mismatched eligibility/support.
limitations: Does not by itself invalidate the separate type-level multiverse or document-cluster bootstrap.

claim: The displayed 0.9 Holm-adjusted p-values are consistent with standard step-down Holm adjustment for the 12 displayed raw p-values.
limitations: Validates correction arithmetic only; does not strengthen the underlying null model.

claim: 2.4.2 establishes a multi-witness representation in which evidential support is counted by source lineage rather than number of digital representations.
limitations: Infrastructure claim; source-by-source population remains incomplete.

claim: The separately frozen statistical repair executed twice with identical result bytes on the historical corpus; the historical 2.5 implementation remains quarantined.
limitations: Candidates were selected on this corpus; corrected diagnostic p-values do not undo selection bias or establish prospective, linguistic or independent confirmation.
